examples.english: This ramen is insanely, dangerously delicious.

examples.kana: しゅくだいをわすれてしまってほんとうにやばいです。
examples.romaji: shukudai o wasurete shimatte hontou ni yabai desu.
examples.english: I forgot my homework and am in serious trouble.

card_50_006.english: A little / just a moment / well... (polite hesitation/declining)
card_50_006.usageNote: Can mean a small amount ("chotto dake"), a quick pause ("chotto matte"), or a gentle, non-confrontational refusal ("sore wa chotto...").

examples.kana: ちょっとまってください、すぐにもどります。
examples.romaji: chotto matte kudasai, sugu ni modorimasu.
examples.english: Just a moment please, I will be right back.

examples.kana: あしたののみかいはちょっとつごうがわるいです。
examples.romaji: ashita no nomikai wa chotto tsugou ga warui desu.
examples.english: Tomorrow's drinking party is a bit inconvenient for me.

examples.kana: スープにちょっとだけしおをくわえました。
examples.romaji: suupu ni chotto dake shio o kuwaemashita.
examples.english: I added just a little bit of salt to the soup.

card_50_007.usageNote: Hesitation filler used while collecting thoughts or searching for information in memory. Friendly and casual.

examples.kana: ええと、つぎのよていはなんじでしたっけ。
examples.romaji: eeto, tsugi no yotei wa nanji deshita kke.
examples.english: Let's see, what time was the next appointment again?

examples.kana: ええと、わたしがいいたいのはそういうことではありません。
examples.romaji: eeto, watashi ga iitai no wa sou iu koto de wa arimasen.
examples.english: Well, what I want to say is not that kind of thing.

examples.kana: ええと、かれのなまえはたしかたなかさんでした。
examples.romaji: eeto, kare no namae wa tashika tanaka-san deshita.
examples.english: Um, his name was Tanaka, if I recall correctly.

card_50_008.english: Um / excuse me / err (polite soft attention-getter)
card_50_008.usageNote: Polite conversational opener when initiating a question, requesting assistance, or showing mild hesitation.

examples.kana: あのう、すみません、えきはどちらでしょうか。
examples.romaji: anou, sumimasen, eki wa dochira deshou ka.
examples.english: Um, excuse me, which way is the train station?

examples.kana: あのう、すこしおじかんをいただいてもよろしいですか。
examples.romaji: anou, sukoshi ojikan o itadaite mo yoroshii desu ka.
examples.english: Um, would it be alright if I borrow a little of your time?

examples.kana: あのう、このかさはあなたのものですか。
examples.romaji: anou, kono kasa wa anata no mono desu ka.
examples.english: Um, is this umbrella yours?

card_50_009.english: Seriously? / No way! / For real? / Honestly
card_50_009.usageNote: Casual colloquial phrase expressing disbelief or earnest emphasis ("maji de?!" = seriously?!; "maji de yabai" = seriously bad/awesome).

examples.kana: まじで！？あしたテストがあるなんてきいてないよ！
examples.romaji: maji de!? ashita tesuto ga aru nante kiite nai yo!
examples.english: Seriously?! I hadn't heard that there was a test tomorrow!

examples.kana: かれがぷろになったとしって、まじでおどろきました。
examples.romaji: kare ga puro ni natta to shitte, maji de odorokimashita.
examples.english: Hearing that he turned pro, I was seriously astonished.

examples.kana: このもんだいはまじでむずかしいとおもいます。
examples.romaji: kono mondai wa maji de muzukashii to omoimasu.
examples.english: I think this problem is seriously difficult.

card_50_010.english: As expected! / That's so like you! / Impressive! / Truly great
card_50_010.usageNote: Compliment acknowledging that someone has lived up to their high reputation or talents ("sasuga desu ne" = just as expected of you!).

examples.kana: ひとりでぜんぶなおしたなんて、さすがですね！
examples.romaji: hitori de zenbu naoshita nante, sasuga desu ne!
examples.english: Fixing everything all by yourself—impressive, as expected!

examples.kana: さすがプロのりょうりにん、あじつけがかんぺきです。
examples.romaji: sasuga puro no ryourinin, ajitsuke ga kampeki desu.
examples.english: Truly a professional chef, the seasoning is flawless.

examples.kana: こんなピンチをのりこえるなんて、さすがパイセンです。
examples.romaji: konna pinchi o norikoeru nante, sasuga paisen desu.
examples.english: Overcoming such a tight spot—that is so like our senior!

card_50_011.english: Of course / certainly / naturally / without doubt
card_50_011.usageNote: Confident affirmation. Used when agreeing readily or stating something obvious ("mochiron desu" = of course!).

examples.kana: あしたのパーティーにきてくれますか。もちろんです！
examples.romaji: ashita no paatii ni kite kuremasu ka. mochiron desu!
examples.english: Will you come to the party tomorrow? Of course!

examples.kana: もちろん、わたしたちもぜんりょくでおてつだいします。
examples.romaji: mochiron, watashitachi mo zenryoku de otetsudai shimasu.
examples.english: Naturally, we will also help out with all our strength.

examples.kana: えいごはもちろん、フランスごもすこしはなせます。
examples.romaji: eigo wa mochiron, furansu-go mo sukoshi hanasemasu.
examples.english: English of course, and I can also speak a little French.

card_50_012.english: Indeed / certainly / that's true / valid point
card_50_012.usageNote: Conceding or confirming the truth of what someone else has pointed out ("tashikani sou desu ne" = indeed, that is true).

examples.kana: たしかにあなたのいうとおりだとおもいます。
examples.romaji: tashikani anata no iu toori da to omoimasu.
examples.english: Indeed, I think it is just as you say.

examples.kana: たしかにそのレストランのりょうりはおいしいです。
examples.romaji: tashikani sono resutoran no ryouri wa oishii desu.
examples.english: Certainly, that restaurant's food is delicious.

examples.kana: たしかにじかんはかかりますが、やるかちはあります。
examples.romaji: tashikani jikan wa kakarimasu ga, yaru kachi wa arimasu.
examples.english: It certainly takes time, but it is worth doing.

card_50_013.english: Ah, I see / got it / is that so?
card_50_013.usageNote: Casual realization marker spoken to oneself or friends when newly understanding a fact. Formal version: "sou desu ka".

examples.kana: そうか、そういうわけだったんだね。
examples.romaji: souka, sou iu wake datta n da ne.
examples.english: Ah I see, so that was the circumstance, wasn't it.

examples.kana: そうか、かれはきょうやすみなんだね。
examples.romaji: souka, kare wa kyou yasumi nan da ne.
examples.english: Got it, so he is off today.

examples.kana: そうか、わたしがかんちがいをしていました。
examples.romaji: souka, watashi ga kanchigai o shite imashita.
examples.english: Ah I see, I was mistaken.

card_50_014.english: Please / go ahead / help yourself / after you
card_50_014.usageNote: Polite invitation or permission offering someone a seat ("douzo osuwari kudasai"), food, or letting them pass first.

examples.kana: こちらのおちゃをどうぞおめしあがりください。
examples.romaji: kochira no ocha o douzo omeshiagari kudasai.
examples.english: Please help yourself to this tea.

examples.kana: おさきにどうぞ、わたしはあとからいきます。
examples.romaji: osaki ni douzo, watashi wa ato kara ikimasu.
examples.english: Please go ahead first; I will come afterwards.

examples.kana: どうぞこちらのおせきにおかけになってください。
examples.romaji: douzo kochira no oseki ni okake ni natte kudasai.
examples.english: Please have a seat in this chair here.

card_50_015.english: Thanks / hello / somehow / in every way
card_50_015.usageNote: Multipurpose social glue. Casual thank you, brief greeting when passing someone, or adverb meaning "somehow" ("doumo umaku ikanai").

examples.kana: どうも、たすかりました、ありがとうございます。
examples.romaji: doumo, tasakarimashita, arigatou gozaimasu.
examples.english: Thanks, you saved me, thank you very much!

examples.kana: どうもこんにちは、おひさしぶりですね。
examples.romaji: doumo konnichiwa, ohisashiburi desu ne.
examples.english: Hello there, long time no see!

examples.kana: きょうはどうもからだのちょうしがよくありません。
examples.romaji: kyou wa doumo karada no choushi ga yoku arimasen.
examples.english: Somehow my physical condition is not great today.

card_50_016.english: As expected / after all / sure enough / just as anticipated
card_50_016.usageNote: Formal/standard version of "yappari". Confirms prior expectations or states an ultimate conclusion after reflection.

examples.kana: よほうどおり、やはりごごからあめがふりはじめました。
examples.romaji: yohou doori, yahari gogo kara ame ga furihajimemashita.
examples.english: As forecasted, sure enough, rain began falling from the afternoon.

examples.kana: いろいろかんがえましたが、やはりこのぷらんがいちばんです。
examples.romaji: iroiro kangaemashita ga, yahari kono puran ga ichiban desu.
examples.english: I considered various options, but after all this plan is best.

examples.kana: やはりかれのいけんがもっともただしいとおもいます。
examples.romaji: yahari kare no iken ga mottomo tadashii to omoimasu.
examples.english: As expected, I think his opinion is the most accurate.

card_50_017.english: As I thought / after all / sure enough (casual spoken form)
card_50_017.usageNote: Everyday conversational equivalent of "yahari". Expresses realization that one's initial hunch was correct.

examples.kana: やっぱり、このケーキがいちばんおいしいね！
examples.romaji: yappari, kono keeki ga ichiban oishii ne!
examples.english: As I thought, this cake is the most delicious!

examples.kana: まよったけれど、やっぱりあおいふくをかうことにしました。
examples.romaji: mayotta keredo, yappari aoi fuku o kau koto ni shimashita.
examples.english: I hesitated, but after all I decided to buy the blue clothes.

examples.kana: やっぱりあのかたがたなかさんのおとうとさんでしたか。
examples.romaji: yappari ano kata ga tanaka-san no otouto-san deshita ka.
examples.english: Just as I thought, was that gentleman Mr. Tanaka's younger brother?

card_50_018.english: And then? / So what happened? / And so... / Therefore
card_50_018.usageNote: Conversation prompter encouraging the speaker to continue their story ("and then?"). Also functions as causal connective "and so".

examples.kana: それで、そのあとどうなったの？はやくおしえて！
examples.romaji: sorede, sono ato dou natta no? hayaku oshiete!
examples.english: And then? What happened after that? Tell me quickly!

examples.kana: でんしゃがおくれました。それでかいぎにおくれてしまいました。
examples.romaji: densha ga okuremashita. sorede kaigi ni okurete shimaimashita.
examples.english: The train was delayed. And so I ended up late for the meeting.

examples.kana: それで、みんなはなんていっていたのですか。
examples.romaji: sorede, minna wa nante itte ita no desu ka.
examples.english: And then, what were all of them saying?

card_50_019.english: Not particularly / nothing really / not especially
card_50_019.usageNote: Used with negative verb constructions to express indifference or non-preference ("betsuni kamawanai" = I don't really mind).

examples.kana: なにかあったの？べつに、なんでもないよ。
examples.romaji: nanika atta no? betsuni, nandemonai yo.
examples.english: Did something happen? Not particularly, it's nothing at all.

examples.kana: べつにいそいではいませんのでごゆっくりどうぞ。
examples.romaji: betsuni isoide wa imasen node goyukkuri douzo.
examples.english: I am not particularly in a hurry, so please take your time.

examples.kana: べつにどこでもいいですよ、すきなばしょをえらんでください。
examples.romaji: betsuni doko demo ii desu yo, sukina basho o erande kudasai.
examples.english: Anywhere is fine really, please choose your favorite spot.

card_50_020.english: Not at all / totally not / absolutely not / entirely
card_50_020.usageNote: Classically used with negatives ("zenzen wakaranai" = don't understand at all). Colloquially also used positively ("zenzen daijoubu" = totally fine).

examples.kana: しんぱいしないでください、ぜんぜんだいじょうぶですよ。
examples.romaji: shinpai shinaide kudasai, zenzen daijoubu desu yo.
examples.english: Please do not worry, I am totally, completely fine!

examples.kana: そのもんだいについてぜんぜんしりませんでした。
examples.romaji: sono mondai ni tsuite zenzen shirimasen deshita.
examples.english: I knew absolutely nothing at all about that problem.

examples.kana: きょうはぜんぜんつかれていません、まだまだげんきです。
examples.romaji: kyou wa zenzen tsukarete imasen, madamada genki desu.
examples.english: I am not tired at all today; I still have plenty of energy.

card_50_021.english: Thank goodness! / That's great! / I'm glad! / What a relief!
card_50_021.usageNote: Past tense of "ii" (good) used as an exclamation of profound relief or congratulations ("yokatta ne!" = I'm so glad for you!).

examples.kana: ぶじにみつかってほんとうによかったです！
examples.romaji: buji ni mitsukatte hontou ni yokatta desu!
examples.english: It was found safely—thank goodness, what a relief!

examples.kana: きょうのてんきがはれてほんとうによかったですね。
examples.romaji: kyou no tenki ga harete hontou ni yokatta desu ne.
examples.english: It's so great that today's weather cleared up nicely.

examples.kana: あなたがげんきそうでほんとうによかったです。
examples.romaji: anata ga genkisou de hontou ni yokatta desu.
examples.english: I am truly glad that you look well and healthy.

card_50_022.english: In trouble / what a dilemma / oh dear / at a loss
card_50_022.usageNote: Past tense of "komaru" used as an exclamation when facing a difficult problem ("komatta na" = oh dear, what should I do?).

examples.kana: かぎをへやのなかにわすれてしまってこまったな。
examples.romaji: kagi o heya no naka ni wasurete shimatte komatta na.
examples.english: I left the key inside the room—oh dear, what a dilemma.

examples.kana: こまったときはいつでもともだちにそうだんしてください。
examples.romaji: komatta toki wa itsudemo tomodachi ni soudan shite kudasai.
examples.english: Whenever you are in trouble, please consult with your friends.

examples.kana: どうすればよいかわからず、みんなでこまりはてました。
examples.romaji: dou sureba yoi ka wakarazu, minna de komarihatemashita.
examples.english: Not knowing what to do, everyone was completely at a loss.

card_50_023.usageNote: Softens an opinion ("maa, daijoubu" = well, it's alright I guess) or acts as an exclamation of mild astonishment ("maa, suteki!" = my, how lovely!).

examples.kana: まあ、そんなにおこらないで、おちついてください。
examples.romaji: maa, sonna ni okoranaide, ochitsuite kudasai.
examples.english: Well, don't get so angry, please calm down.

examples.kana: このしごとはまあまあうまくすすんでいます。
examples.romaji: kono shigoto wa maa-maa umaku susunde imasu.
examples.english: This work is progressing moderately well.

examples.kana: まあ、なんてきれいなはなでしょう！
examples.romaji: maa, nante kireina hana deshou!
examples.english: My goodness, what a lovely flower!

card_50_024.english: Impossible! / No way! / Unbelievable! / Out of the question
card_50_024.usageNote: Negative potential of "aru" (to exist). Colloquial reaction to something absurd, shocking, or completely unthinkable.

examples.kana: そんなことがおきるなんて、ほんとうにありえないよ！
examples.romaji: sonna koto ga okiru nante, hontou ni arienai yo!
examples.english: For such a thing to happen—that is truly impossible!

examples.kana: まいあさよじにおきるなんてわたしにはありえません。
examples.romaji: maiasa yoji ni okiru nante watashi ni wa ariemasen.
examples.english: Waking up at 4 a.m. every morning is out of the question for me!

examples.kana: ありえないミスをしてしまってとてもはんせいしています。
examples.romaji: arienai misu o shite shimatte totemo hansei shite imasu.
examples.english: I made an unbelievable mistake and am deeply regretting it.

card_50_025.english: Well then / in that case / see you then / bye
card_50_025.usageNote: Conversational contraction of "dewa". Used when transitioning, making a conclusion ("jaa sou shiyou"), or saying goodbye ("jaa mata").

examples.kana: じかんになりましたね。じゃあ、またあしたあいましょう！
examples.romaji: jikan ni narimashita ne. jaa, mata ashita aimashou!
examples.english: The time has come. Well then, let us meet again tomorrow!

examples.kana: じゃあ、らいしゅうのげつようびにまたれんらくしますね。
examples.romaji: jaa, raishuu no getsuyoubi ni mata renraku shimasu ne.
examples.english: Well then, I will contact you again next Monday.

examples.kana: あめがふってきたね。じゃあ、タクシーでかえろうか。
examples.romaji: ame ga futte kita ne. jaa, takushii de kaerou ka.
examples.english: Rain started falling. In that case, shall we go home by taxi?
